Constitution, By-Laws, and University Manual Committee (CBUM)

Constitution, By-laws, and University Manual Committee shall comprise four or more members. This committee shall review the operation of University governance and propose changes in the Constitution and By-Laws of the Faculty Senate and in the University Manual; review proposals for changes in University governance from whatever source and make recommendations concerning them to the Faculty Senate and to the other appropriate bodies and individuals; construe the meaning of the Constitution, the By-Laws and the University Manual upon the request of the Senate President or Executive Committee, any senator or member of the General Faculty, or the President; assure that all duly approved changes are incorporated into the Constitution and By-Laws and into the University Manual, and that no unauthorized changes are made in these instruments; and assure that the language of all duly approved changes is consistent with the style, format and arrangement of the Constitution and By-Laws and of the University Manual. #17-18-12 , #20-21-5 , #20-21-14, #20-21-36, #21-22-37

Elimination of Partial Outcomes from the General Education Program (Amends Sections 8.20.12 and 8.20.14 within Chapter 8 of the University Manual) - 2

Introduction.
The motion to formally introduce the proposal was seconded and approved.
Senate President Williams provided background on the initiative, including details of the various committees and administrative offices that have reviewed it or are currently doing so.
He explained that the Partial Outcomes are problematic in a variety of ways.
They are widely misunderstood by both students and faculty, they are not assessable, they are not listed, tracked, or maintained in Ecampus, and given that the university’s reaccreditation review is coming up, it is particularly important that the institution’s goals for the general education program align with its operations.
The proposal will be on the November agenda for a vote.

Clarify requirements related to Graduating with Distinction - (Amends Section 8.22.40 within Chapter 8 of the University Manual) - The motion to formally introduce the proposal was seconded and approved.

College of Education Dean Dennis provided some background, noting that this issue first arose from a series of complaints from students and parents who were surprised at the last minute by an ineligibility for distinction.
Dean Dennis and many of her colleagues agreed that this disappointment is not a circumstance the university should want its new alumni to find themselves in.
The solution was a simple, one-sentence fix in Chapter 8 of the University Manual.
During discussion concerns from the floor were raised about the potential for grade inflation, and whether or not this change might diminish the accomplishments of those students who never had to repeat a course.
There was also concern that while this proposal on its own may have a negligible impact, when combined with passage of related legislation (Item iv below), the number of affected students would increase.
Sen.
Van Wyk noted initial estimates are that this would still be a small number but more data from enrollment services can be made available at the November meeting.
The proposal will be docketed for a November 20 vote. iv.

Aligning URI’s second-grade option (SGO) provisions with peer institutions (Amends Section 8.33.32 within Chapter 8 of the University Manual, allowing students to avail themselves of SGO at any time during their undergraduate careers) - The motion to formally introduce the proposal was seconded and approved.
FSEC Member Meenach presented the proposal and reminded senators that there had been a robust discussion on the proposal last month.
Questions from the floor sought to address implementation matters, especially regarding when the bill would take effect.
AVP for Enrollment Services Humphrey offered that options seemed open regarding whether this change could become effective for students currently enrolled, or if it would apply to those newly enrolling in Fall, 2026.
The Senate would need to decide, upon approving the legislation, which effective date to assign.
AVP Humphrey also noted that implementation would likely take considerable effort in his office to code the “repeat rules” for specific second grade pursuits.

FSEC members added that URI is more restrictive than its peer institutions in regard to the second grade option and FSEC is working with UCAS to address any comments or concerns they may forward.
Senators and faculty generally were encouraged to send other comments directly to FSEC members so their concerns might be addressed before the bill is offered for adoption at the November meeting.

Nicole King, faculty member in the College of Education noted, joined by several of her colleagues, that the calendar is a values statement and if the university states that its mission is to provide an inclusive and diverse experience for its students, it should honor the holiday.
Senate Vice President Preisser noted that there was precedent for using the holiday as an instructional day when the calendar does not otherwise provide enough instructional days during the fall semester.

ACC Chair Donnelly explained that such legislation would be welcome, but the preparers should bear in mind that in some years, there simply are not enough days between Labor Day and the end of the term, and a holiday will need to be sacrificed in order to secure an adequate number of class meetings. ii.
Discussion of spring 2026 late semester adjustments - Pres.
Williams explained that the four snow days experienced so far this year mean that the university must consider adding a day of instruction (make-up day for Monday classes).
He outlined four options that included such possibilities as using a Saturday for instruction or exams, asynchronous instruction on Reading Day, and starting and ending exams a day later than the published calendar currently reflects.
There was considerable debate and it was noted that some disciplines and modalities are more impacted than others.
It was further noted that doing nothing (leaving the calendar as-is) is also an option.
Faculty were invited to share their preferences and rationals with Faculty Senate leaders and the Provost’s office.

Any change to the calendar at this point would be subject to a vote by the senate, either at the April meeting or before that via special called session (virtual), with confirmation by the full Senate to follow. g.
Service and Community Life Committee - Informational Report on the University Ombuds - Committee Member Bevan provided some background information on the effort to modernize the office of the Ombuds and noted that actual University Manual language will be available at the April meeting.
Such Manual language will include a slight change to the By-Laws, which requires consideration by the senate in two separate meetings.
The affected language was introduced.
In brief, the Ombuds office provides independent, impartial, informal, and confidential resources for faculty, staff, and students; to address concerns, conflicts, and systemic issues.
Ombuds are guided by the International Ombuds Association Standards of Practice and their office would be structurally housed under the office of the University President. 5

7. CALL for NEW BUSINESS Introduction - Internal-Facing Survey Assistance launch - FSEC member Van Wyk provided some background on the need for survey assistance to be provided and noted that a goal of the project is to improve the quality of feedback and data collected and used by university leaders. She encouraged all faculty to explore the web resources available via the Faculty Senate webpage and to volunteer to assist if they have expertise in this area. Any survey assistance provided as part of this initiative would count as service. In other new business, an inquiry was made regarding the delayed issuance of W-2’s this year and the need for subsequent corrections. It was noted that W-2’s are not issued by the University but by the State Department of Administration, but the Human Resources office is ready and available to assist faculty and staff who have concerns or questions. 8.
